name: Seam Welding & Structural Reinforcement
description: Stitch/seam welding of factory spot-welded seams and local reinforcement plates at high-load hard points (strut towers, cradle mounts, cage feet). Done on the bare shell before cage installation and paint.

components.name: Front structure stitch welds (rails, aprons, strut towers, dash)
components.description: Short MIG stitch welds added between factory spot welds along the front rail flanges, the strut-tower-to-apron seams, the tower-to-rail joint and the dash-to-tower junction. This prevents spot-weld peel and seam slip under racing loads and raises torsional stiffness, especially at the front where the Gen 6 strut towers carry the full front spring/damper load.
components.location: Engine bay: front rails, strut towers (x approx -0.1 to 0.2, y 0.5-0.85, z +/-0.5), dash/cowl junction.

factory.name: Factory spot welds + structural adhesive
factory.notes: GM uses spot welds and structural adhesive. Adhesive and sealer must be ground/burned away locally before stitch welding (fumes are toxic; ventilate and wear a respirator).

raceOptions.name: Stitch weld pattern: 25 mm (1 in) bead every 50-75 mm, alternating sides
raceOptions.notes: Short, cool stitches minimize heat distortion and burn-through of thin (0.7-1.2 mm) sheet. Fully continuous seams are not necessary and add distortion/weight.

specs.Prep: Strip seam sealer, adhesive and e-coat to bright metal 10 mm each side

installNotes: Measure the shell (cradle mount diagonals, tower-to-tower) before welding and fixture/brace the body so it cannot move.
Strip sealer and paint along each seam with a wire wheel / stripping disc; remove adhesive with heat gun and scraper.
Weld in a skip pattern, alternating side-to-side and front-to-rear to spread heat; let areas cool before continuing.
Re-measure, then re-seal seams with seam sealer and prime (see chassis.corrosion-and-coatings).
inspection: Inspect weld toes at strut towers for cracking after first race weekend and every few events thereafter.

modelRef.features: 25 mm MIG stitches along the tower/apron seams

components.name: Underbody stitch welds (floor-to-rocker, tunnel, seat cross-members)
components.description: Stitch welds along the floor-to-rocker seam, floor-to-tunnel seams and seat cross-member flanges, done mostly from inside the cockpit with the interior stripped. These seams carry the main torsional shear path between front and rear structures.

specs.Process: MIG stitch, same parameters as front structure

installNotes: Remove all deadener first (dry ice or heat gun + scraper).
Remove fuel and brake lines from the underside before welding near them, or shield them; route new lines after welding (phase 2).
inspection: Check for cracking near cage feet and seat mounts.

components.name: Rear structure stitch welds (rear rails, shock towers, wheelhouses)
components.description: Stitch welds at the rear rail flanges, rear wheelhouse-to-shock-tower seams and the rear floor kick-up. The rear cradle bushings and braces feed tractive and cornering loads into this area.
components.location: Rear wheelhouses and trunk, x approx 2.4-3.3.
installNotes: Remove fuel tank, rear cradle and all trim from the rear area before welding.
inspection: Check rear cradle mount areas for cracking.

components.name: Cradle mount reinforcement plates (front and rear)
components.description: Steel doubler/spreader plates welded around the front and rear cradle mounting points on the rails. Recommended when the cradles are solid-mounted (rubber isolators removed), because the body then sees sharper load peaks at these 8 points.
components.location: Front cradle mounts approx (x -0.38 and 0.12, y 0.30, z +/-0.42); rear cradle mounts approx (x 2.45 and 3.08, y 0.40, z +/-0.48).

factory.name: None (factory relies on rail section and captured nut plate)

raceOptions.name: Fabricated 3-4 mm (0.120-0.160 in) steel doubler plates
raceOptions.notes: Plug weld + perimeter stitch; keep the captured-nut bore concentric and do not distort the nut plate.

installNotes: Install the cradle loosely (with bolts) before welding the plates to keep holes aligned; remove cradle before final welding.
inspection: Check for cracking at plate perimeters.

modelRef.features: Doublers around each cradle bolt on the body rails

components.name: Strut tower reinforcement / gussets
components.description: Plates or gussets welded to the inside of the front strut towers and between tower and rail/apron, and a reinforcing ring around the top-mount area. Especially important with camber plates (load is offset) and with hard-mounted race top mounts.
components.location: Front strut towers, x approx 0.05, y 0.6-0.85, z +/-0.55.

raceOptions.name: Fabricated tower top doubler with cage tie-in tab
raceOptions.notes: Keep 3-bolt top-mount pattern and the camber-plate slot clear.

installNotes: Trial-fit camber plates and strut tower brace before welding reinforcement so bolt holes and clearances are maintained.
inspection: Look for cracks around the top-mount bolt holes.

modelRef.features: Tower-top doubler with centre hole and 3 stud holes

components.name: Roll-cage mounting / backing plates (body interface)
components.description: Steel landing plates welded to floor, rockers, A/B pillars and rear shock towers to receive the cage feet. The plates spread cage loads into the unibody. Sizes and thickness are set by the governing rulebook (NASA CCR / SCCA GCR cage rules specify minimum plate area and thickness).
components.location: Main hoop feet near B-pillar (x approx 2.1, z +/-0.75), front hoop/A-pillar feet (x approx 0.85), rear down-bar feet at rear shock towers (x approx 2.75).

raceOptions.name: Plates per rulebook (typically >= 0.080-0.125 in steel, >= 16-36 sq in depending on rules)
raceOptions.notes: Confirm exact minimums in the current NASA CCR / SCCA GCR before cutting plates.

installNotes: Owned jointly with the safety system; welded during chassis prep (phase 1) before paint.
inspection: Check plate welds during annual tech.
